title: CICC warns vs. posts 'seemingly' promoting violence amid ASEAN Summit
summary: The CICC on Monday said it is monitoring online content that "seemingly" encourages violence amid ongoing protests as the country hosts the 2026 ASEAN Summit.

blocks.text: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) on Monday said it is monitoring online content that "seemingly" encourages violence amid ongoing protests as the country hosts the 2026 ASEAN Summit.

“We respect the public’s right to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, and to seek redress from the government. But these freedoms should never be used as justification to incite violence or threaten public safety,” said CICC executive director Renato Paraiso in a statement.
The agency said it identified individuals whose online posts "seemingly promote or incite violence" in connection to the protests.
The CICC added that it is still assessing the credibility of the said posts.

"While the government recognizes the public’s right to air grievances and participate in peaceful protests, it will not tolerate attempts to incite violence or provoke unrest through online platforms," the agency added.
Over 200 protesters from Southern Tagalog were arrested in Sucat, Parañaque, during a protest caravan and were brought to Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City as ASEAN Summit 2026 opened on Sunday.
Among the apprehended individuals, 19 are reportedly minors. The Southern Police District, however, said the minors were rescued rather than arrested.
Various organization have condemned the arrests and the alleged violent dispersal of protesters in Metro Manila on Sunday. — BM, GMA News
